card.text: A spiral galaxy 9.4 million parsecs away, seen close to edge-on.

Wikipedia, "Sombrero Galaxy"
sources.quote: The Sombrero Galaxy is a peculiar galaxy of unclear classification in the constellation borders of Virgo and Corvus, being about 9.55 megaparsecs from the Milky Way galaxy.

introduction.text: Its picture is the Sloan Digital Sky Survey's, with the Milky Way's foreground stars removed, standing as a flat picture that faces the Sun.

sources.label: Sloan Digital Sky Survey; color HiPS CDS/P/SDSS9/color by T. Boch (CDS), cut out by the CDS hips2fits service
Wikipedia, "Sombrero Galaxy"
sources.quote: It is a member of the Virgo II Groups, a series of galaxies and galaxy clusters strung out from the southern edge of the Virgo Supercluster.

optical.title: Sombrero Galaxy in visible light
optical.summary: Visible-light image on a flat plane facing the Sun; nothing in it has depth.
